title: Support Customizable Keyboard Shortcuts for Command Palette Input
author: axgn
summary: Command Palette uses fixed input-editing and result-navigation key handling; the request is a clear candidate for a scoped keybinding design.

status.label: Design investigation queued
status.detail: The requested behavior is specific to the focused Command Palette input and the current implementation has explicit hard-coded handlers for navigation and editing-related keys, so design can proceed without more reporter evidence.

evidence: The reporter names concrete command categories: result navigation, word deletion, and deletion to the beginning of the line.
The requested bindings apply only while the Command Palette input field is focused.
SearchBar.xaml.cs handles Escape, Backspace, arrow keys, Page Up, and Page Down directly and sends semantic navigation commands.
judgment.recommended_action: Queue a focused design for configurable semantic input commands, conflict validation, defaults, and accessibility while retaining existing key behavior by default.

issue_context.summary: Command Palette uses fixed input-editing and result-navigation key handling; the request is a clear candidate for a scoped keybinding design.
known_information: The request is for configurable Vim-style or Emacs-style bindings only in the Command Palette input field.
Current Command Palette input handling maps several physical keys directly to navigation or editing behavior.
No assignee or linked implementation is present on the live issue.
inferences: A semantic command-to-keybinding layer could likely cover the request more safely than arbitrary keystroke remapping.
The design will need conflict rules so text editing, result navigation, and extension-provided shortcuts do not consume the same chord.
issue_context.analysis: The issue supplies enough product intent and scope for design. Repository inspection identifies the current key-handling seam, but a full design still needs to define which commands are configurable and how conflicts and reserved text-editing behavior are resolved.
initial_investigation: src/modules/cmdpal/Microsoft.CmdPal.UI/Controls/SearchBar.xaml.cs contains direct handlers for Escape, Backspace, arrows, Page Up, and Page Down.
The handlers already emit navigation messages such as NavigatePreviousCommand and NavigateNextCommand, providing a semantic boundary for future configuration.
No duplicate or active owner was exposed by the issue timeline.
